summary: Monday closed with the picture established earlier holding firm: the S&P 500 finished at 7,652.86 down 0.28% while the Dow held positive at 53,417.16 up 0.26%, confirming a rotation out of growth and into defensives rather than a broad market breakdown. What sharpened through the afternoon was the severity of the tech damage, with Technology closing at 180.05 down 2.01% and the Nasdaq 100 at 706.32 down 1.12%, while Consumer Staples at 87.45 up 1.67% and Financials at 58.22 up 1.23% absorbed the money that left chips and software. The VIX closed at 15.85 up 4.76%, a meaningful single day tick higher that signals hedging demand increased into the close, though it does not yet represent alarm. Bitcoin finished at 80,594.93 up 2.04% and gold settled at 4,695.40 down 0.17%, with the 10 year yield at 4.70 down 0.72% meaning bond buyers were active. The biggest single stock story was IONQ collapsing 8.04% and MU falling 5.53%, both in the portfolio, alongside broad weakness in memory and AI adjacent names. The critical week ahead delivers Core PCE on Wednesday, preliminary GDP on Wednesday, unemployment claims Thursday, and Fed Chair Warsh speaking Friday alongside the preliminary benchmark payrolls revision.
